title: Generate a new locale on Arch Linux
summary: Before you can use a specific language or region setting, you must generate it on your system. This involves editing a configuration file and running a command.

steps.explain: Open the locale generation configuration file. You need to uncomment the line corresponding to the locale you want to enable (e.g., `en_US.UTF-8 UTF-8` or `de_DE.UTF-8 UTF-8`).
steps.gui: Open /etc/locale.gen with a text editor as root. Remove the '#' at the start of the line for your desired locale.

steps.explain: Run the locale generation command to apply the changes made in the configuration file.

rollback.explain: To undo, comment out the line you previously uncommented in /etc/locale.gen and run locale-gen again.
rollback.gui: Open /etc/locale.gen with a text editor as root. Add a '#' at the start of the line for the locale you want to disable.

rollback.explain: Regenerate locales to remove the disabled one.

warnings: Ensure you keep `en_US.UTF-8 UTF-8` uncommented as a fallback for many system tools.
UTF-8 is recommended over other character sets.
